title: The Hidden Physics of GPS
hook: What if your GPS was wrong by ten kilometers every day?
script: What if your GPS was wrong by ten kilometers every day? GPS satellites orbit at 20,200 kilometers, moving at 14,000 kilometers per hour. This speed causes their atomic clocks to tick faster, gaining about 38 microseconds daily. The satellites are farther from Earth's gravity, which also speeds up their clocks. Over a million days, that adds up to a staggering 38 seconds of time gained. Each time you follow a map, your phone silently adjusts for these time differences. Reality bends around you, and you remain blissfully unaware.
